description:
Brandywine Meadows is within a Grizzly Bear Wildlife Habitat Area. It contains high value habitat which is used by several sow Grizzly Bears each year to raise their cubs. No Camping is permitted along the trail, and camping not recommended in the surrounding area.

Summer hikhing trail only, approx. 6km round trip. This trail starts off from the Brandywine Forest Service Road. It is steep for the first hour, through a stand of large Western Red cedar and yellow cedar, and levels out in the sub alpine. The meadows have great views of Blacktusk and the valley below. Alpine meadow flowers in bloom for much of the summer. A nice cold creek trickles off the glacier, perfect for cooling off hot feet!
directions: Follow the Brandywine Forest Service road to the end (4x4 required or park at the bottom of the big hill near the end if you only have 2WD), where there is a deactivated bridge and an outhouse and sign kiosk-the trailhead is just behind the sign kiosk up the large rocks. Access to the Branydwine Forest Service road is off of the Callaghan Valley road, on HWY 99, 4 km norht of the Brandywine Provincial Park.
title: Brandywine Meadows
